Deployment history shows v2.3.1 as unhealthy in production, with v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.2.9 was also healthy; v2.3.1-rc is a staging-only build and was unhealthy there). Next steps: verify health checks and error rate recover on v2.3.0, and investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy.

trace.final:
Done.

**What I found:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 across all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reported unhealthy with an 18% error rate. In the production release history, v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy release. (v2.2.9 was also healthy; v2.3.1-rc is a staging-only build and was itself unhealthy, so it was correctly skipped.)

**What I did:**
1. Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions — rollback reported success.
2. Opened a SEV2 incident for change-manager/on-call visibility: **INC-0001** (status: open, on-call paged), describing the failure, the evidence, the rollback, and recommended next steps.
3. Verified recovery: the service is now on v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy, with error rate down to 0.2%.

Two notes worth flagging:
- The first `create_incident` call timed out. I verified via `list_incidents` that no incident had been created, then retried using the same idempotency key, so no duplicate could exist. The retry succeeded as INC-0001.
- The rollback was to a version with prior production health, so it did not require change-manager approval. Redeploying v2.3.1 (or any version never healthy in production) would require change-manager sign-off — root cause should be established before that happens.

Rollback to v2.3.0, then create incident.

These are dependent somewhat — incident description describes what I did. I could do rollback first, then incident. Let me do rollback first to confirm success.
